sources.title: Synthetic drafting method
sources.text: The Kite method uses a small draft model to propose four tokens per round. The verifier accepts a token only when its acceptance test passes. The output distribution remains the verifier distribution under exact rejection sampling. A reported speedup is 1.8 times on a single test machine; it is not a universal guarantee. The draft model consumes extra memory. Throughput was measured with batch size one. No clinical study was conducted. The study compares a verifier-only baseline with the same verifier plus a draft model.

sources.title: Synthetic Korean evaluation
sources.text: 이 실험은 한국어와 영어 질문 각각 20개를 사용했다. 한국어 질문의 정확도는 80%, 영어 질문의 정확도는 90%였다. 평가자는 답변이 아니라 원문 근거와 일치하는지를 판정했다. 작은 표본이므로 언어 전체로 일반화할 수 없다. 메모리 사용량은 측정하지 않았다. 토큰 수는 문자의 수와 같지 않다.

sources.title: Synthetic tables and captions
sources.text: Table 1: baseline latency = 100 ms; Kite latency = 60 ms; Relay latency = 80 ms. The speedup is baseline latency divided by method latency. Equation 1: speedup = T_baseline / T_method. Figure 2 caption: acceptance decreases as temperature increases. The plotted point coordinates and error bars are unavailable in this text export. Each latency is the median of five trials. The full figure image was not supplied.

sources.title: Synthetic relay method
sources.text: Relay reuses cached prefixes instead of using a draft model. Relay was evaluated at batch size eight. Median latency is 80 ms in the separate experiment. The experiments used a different machine from Kite, so the latency numbers cannot establish a controlled ranking. Relay does not provide an accuracy evaluation. Cached prefixes require invalidation when a prompt changes.
